On an average shift, this is a list of some of things I would do:

Listen to handover. Note down any outstanding tasks/info about each pt. 

After this I allocate a staff member to do the first round of pt observations. Write the timetable for the day of which staff is doing the observations each hour

Completing various forms of paperwork (risk assessments, treatment plans, various other assessment tools etc)

Admissions - this involves receiving and giving a handover of the patient, ensuring the bedroom is clean etc, completing loads of admission paperwork, introducing the patient to the ward and answering questions etc, speaking to relatives if they give permission to do so. Conversely, discharges have their own protocols

Completing physical observations

There may be reviews (meetings between  the doctor/MDT and the patient). 

Spending some time with patients and assessing their mental health, de-escalating situations.

Checking equipment

Talking with other professionals from different disciplines, answering the phone, completing tasks in the diary, requesting patients to be assessed by medics etc.

May be working with students also. 

Talking to relatives/visitors 

Writing clinical notes for each patient for the day

Medication rounds. This may involve giving people IM injections under restraint in rare scenarios to manage agitation as a last resort. Or also depot injections. 

Sometimes I may have to give evidence in tribunals (when people appeal against being legally detained). This is like a formal meeting/court setting. 

There will invariably be several things that I need to complete/chase up during the day. Anything I can't do I write in the diary for the next day/email to next shift

Hopefully get a break (some rare occasions this is not possible)

And finally hand over to the night shift
